question_text: A ray of light strikes on a glass sphere at point A. If A is midway between P and Q, then the deviation of the ray as it emerges out of the sphere will be:
solution: Angle of incidence at point A is $45^\circ$. Using $\mu = \sqrt{2}$, $\sin r = \frac{\sin 45^\circ}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{2} \implies r = 30^\circ$. Total deviation $\delta = 2(i - r) = 2(45^\circ - 30^\circ) = 30^\circ$.

question_text: A thin lens of focal length $10\text{ cm}$ is cut into two equal halves and are kept as shown in figure. If an object O is placed at distance $10\text{ cm}$ from the optical centre of combination, then the distance of image from object will be:
solution: Each half cut along the principal axis retains focal length $f = 10\text{ cm}$. In contact, $F = 5\text{ cm}$. Since the object is at $u = -10\text{ cm} = -2F$, the image is at $v = +2F = 10\text{ cm}$. Total distance = $10 + 10 = 20\text{ cm}$.

question_text: The average value of focal length of a normal human eye-lens is approximately:
solution: The distance between the eye-lens and the retina in a normal human eye is approximately $2\text{ cm}$.

question_text: What should be the angle between two plane mirrors, if an object placed unsymmetrically between them has five images?
solution: For unsymmetrical placement with an odd integer $m = \frac{360^\circ}{\theta}$, the number of images is $n = m$. Thus, $\frac{360^\circ}{\theta} = 5 \implies \theta = 72^\circ$.

question_text: A converging spherical wavefront is obtained from:
options: Light emerging from a convex lens when a point source is placed at its focus
A parallel beam of light incident on the convex lens
solution: A parallel beam focused by a convex lens converges to the focus, and any light beam converging towards a point forms a converging spherical wavefront.

question_text: A ray is incident normally on a right angled prism whose refractive index is $\sqrt{3}$ and prism angle $\alpha = 30^\circ$. Deviation to the ray is equal to:
solution: At the first face, $r_1 = 0$, so at the second face the angle of incidence is $r_2 = \alpha = 30^\circ$. By Snell's law: $\sqrt{3}\sin 30^\circ = \sin e \implies e = 60^\circ$. Deviation $\delta = e - r_2 = 60^\circ - 30^\circ = 30^\circ = \frac{\pi}{6}$.

question_text: A convex lens forms an image of a point object O on the screen. If a glass slab of thickness $3\text{ cm}$ and refractive index $1.5$ is introduced before the lens, then to have the image of the object on the screen again, the object should be shifted:
options: Away from the lens by $1\text{ cm}$
Away from the lens by $1.5\text{ cm}$
solution: Normal shift by slab is $\Delta x = t\left(1 - \frac{1}{\mu}\right) = 3\left(1 - \frac{1}{1.5}\right) = 1\text{ cm}$ towards the lens. To restore the apparent position, the object must be moved 1 cm away from the lens.
